description:
Atoms are over 99.9999999% empty space. If you squeezed out all that empty space, every person on Earth would fit inside a single sugar cube!

hook: Right now, your entire body is mostly empty space.
question: So if atoms are mostly empty, why do your feet stop on the floor instead of falling right through? What force is pushing back? Tell me your guess below!
answer_comment: The answer: The Pauli Exclusion Principle and electromagnetic forces! Electrons cannot occupy the same quantum state. When the electron clouds in your shoes and the floor overlap, quantum mechanics forces them into higher energy states, generating immense repulsive resistance. You're essentially levitating on a tiny cushion of electromagnetic repulsion governed by the Pauli Exclusion Principle! What crazy physics fact should we explore next?

topic: Why does ice float when almost every other solid sinks in its own liquid
title: Why Does Ice Float?
description:
Ever wonder why ice cubes float instead of sinking? It comes down to the unique way water molecules behave when they freeze. Explore the science of density! #science #physics #shorts

Video by Afzaal0001 on Pixabay
Video by Hans on Pixabay
Video by Kaffeesüchtig on Pixabay
Video by Kanenori on Pixabay
Video by MilanWulf on Pixabay
Video by Razzak_100 on Pixabay
Video by RoyBuri on Pixabay
hook: Many things shrink when they freeze, but water is one of the few that actually expands.
question: Ever thought how this trick of nature keeps fish alive in a frozen lake?
answer_comment: The answer: Because ice is less dense than water, it forms a solid layer on the surface of the lake. This top layer of ice actually acts like a blanket, insulating the deeper water from the freezing air above. This keeps the water below the ice liquid, so fish can swim through the winter. Pretty cool, right? Got another question about the states of matter?

topic: Why Farmed Salmon Is Naturally Gray While Wild Salmon Is Bright Pink
title: Why Farmed Salmon Is Naturally Gray 🐟🤔
description:
Ever wonder why store-bought salmon is always bright pink, even though the fish starts out gray? We dive into the science of pigments and farm-raised diets. #shorts #foodscience #salmon

Video by Eaktas06 on Pixabay
Video by GreenCardShow on Pixabay
Video by JayShawflybydrones on Pixabay
Video by Kaffeesüchtig on Pixabay
Video by LisaOlivia on Pixabay
Video by XiaosKitchen on Pixabay
Video by dslr99 on Pixabay
hook: Your salmon dinner would actually be much paler without its diet.
narration: Your salmon dinner would actually be much paler without its diet. In the wild, salmon get their signature pink color from eating tiny crustaceans like krill and shrimp. These creatures are packed with a natural red pigment called astaxanthin. But farmed salmon eat a diet of fish pellets without those red pigments. Think about what happens if you feed a bird colored dye; what do you think fish farmers do to get that pink color back? Pause and guess... three, two, one. Here’s why: farmers add the exact same pigment—astaxanthin—to the feed to match the consumer's expectation of pink salmon. It’s not just fish; flamingos get their color from the same source. Ever thought why a bright pink egg yolk is sometimes considered a sign of a healthier chicken? Drop your guess below.
question: Ever thought why a bright pink egg yolk is sometimes considered a sign of a healthier chicken?
answer_comment: The answer: Just like salmon, chickens get their egg yolk color from the pigments in their diet! If a chicken eats plenty of plants rich in carotenoids—like corn, marigolds, or alfalfa—their yolks turn a deep, vibrant orange. If they eat a plain diet like wheat or barley, the yolks stay pale yellow. It shows that the 'health' of the egg is tied to the variety of the chicken's diet. Ever thought how your own skin might change color if you ate only carrots for a month?

topic: Why 99% of the 'Wasabi' You Eat Is Just Dyed Horseradish
title: Why Your Sushi Wasabi Is A Lie 🍣🧪
description:
Think that green paste at your favorite sushi spot is the real deal? Think again. We explore why authentic wasabi is rarely what you're actually eating.

#foodscience #sushi #learnontiktok

Photo by emilyralston on Pixabay
Video by Kanenori on Pixabay
Video by XiaosKitchen on Pixabay
Video by klimkin on Pixabay
hook: That green paste on your sushi plate is almost certainly a lie.
narration: That green paste on your sushi plate is almost certainly a lie. Authentic wasabi is a finicky root that grows in cold, running mountain water. It’s so expensive and hard to farm that it rarely leaves Japan. Most 'wasabi' is actually just horseradish mixed with mustard and green dye. Now, why does the fake stuff hit your nose so hard compared to the real thing? Think about how flavor compounds evaporate. Pause and guess... three, two, one. Here's why: real wasabi's heat is subtle and fades in minutes. Horseradish chemicals are much more stable and aggressive, so they linger. Ever thought why a raw onion makes your eyes sting, even though it's not even in your mouth? Drop your guess below.
question: Ever thought why a raw onion makes your eyes sting, even though it's not even in your mouth?
answer_comment: The answer: Both onions and horseradish/wasabi use volatile chemical compounds to defend themselves from being eaten. When you cut an onion, you break its cells, releasing enzymes that create a gas. This gas drifts through the air, hits the moisture in your eyes, and creates a mild acid that causes that stinging sensation! It's a natural chemical defense system. Any other foods that make you cry?

topic: Sea Otters Have 1 Million Hairs Per Square Inch (Why They Never Get Wet)
title: Why Sea Otters Never Get Wet 🦦❄️
description:
Sea otters don't have blubber like whales, so they rely on the densest fur in the animal kingdom to survive. See how they trap air to stay warm in the freezing ocean. #shorts #science #animals

Photo by Janvanbizar on Pixabay
Photo by Sunriseforever on Pixabay
Photo by ambquinn on Pixabay
Video by GreenCardShow on Pixabay
Video by estivejovem on Pixabay
Video by stefaniejockschat on Pixabay
hook: Sea otters have one million hairs per square inch, and it is one of the main reasons they stay warm, alongside their incredibly high metabolism.
narration: Sea otters have one million hairs per square inch, and it is one of the main reasons they stay warm, alongside their incredibly high metabolism. That is roughly five hundred times denser than the hair on your own head. Their fur is so incredibly packed that water rarely reaches their skin, keeping their undercoat mostly dry. But here is the weird part: if they stay dry, why do they spend hours every single day aggressively rubbing and blowing air into their coat? Think about what happens to your clothes when you trap air inside the fibers. Pause and guess... three, two, one. Here's why: that trapped air is an insulator that prevents the freezing ocean water from drawing heat away from their body. Without those air pockets, they would lose body heat very rapidly. Ever thought how a thick wool sweater keeps you warm, even if it gets slightly damp? Drop your guess below.
question: Ever thought how a thick wool sweater keeps you warm, even if it gets slightly damp? Drop your guess below.
answer_comment: The answer: Wool fibers are naturally crimped, which traps tiny pockets of air to insulate you. Even when damp, wool keeps you warm because the fibers absorb moisture, releasing a small amount of heat in the process, and their structure keeps them from matting down and losing their loft.
